runs.name: PEDEVCO Corp.; NYSE American PED, an onshore oil and gas producer focused on legacy proven properties in the D-J Basin, the Powder River Basin and the Permian San Andres; formerly Blast Energy Services, renamed on the reverse acquisition of Pacific Energy Development in 2012; North Peak Oil & Gas and Century Oil and Gas Sub-Holdings bought 2025-10-31 for cash and Series A preferred, converted into 8,506,818 common shares 2026-02-27; 1-for-20 reverse split 2026-03-13; Civitas, SM Energy and Evolution Petroleum read as the basin operators the 10-K names
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$13.48** (2026-10-15 close, `tools/run.py`'s live quote, aggregator, flagged). Shares: 13,290,902 common, one class (10-Q to 2026-06-30, 0001654954-26-007591, `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing, no treasury shares; after the 8,506,818-share conversion of the Series A preferred on 2026-02-27 and the 1-for-20 reverse split of 2026-03-13); market cap $179.2M. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15, issuing authority). Filing read: 10-K FY2025, 0001654954-26-003098, operating cash FY2025 $10,758 thousand cross-checked against the filed statement; 10-Ks FY2019 and FY2021 to FY2024, both 2026 10-Qs, the proxy, the DEFM14C on the mergers and the 2026 8-Ks. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), stated in the run file. `tools/run.py`'s capex-basis owner earnings found wrong for this filer (a vehicle-purchase tag taken as capital spending, overstating owner cash by about $17M to $35M a year) and not used; figures by hand. Q1 IN (an onshore price-taking producer of oil, about 72% of proved reserves, gas and NGLs in the D-J, Powder River and Permian San Andres, read off its figures). **Q2 OUT**: a high-cost producer in a commodity field, shown on its own and its basin neighbours' filings over a full oil cycle: unit production cost $8.98 to $19.77 a Boe 2017 to 2025, 1.5 to 4.2 times Civitas's and SM Energy's in every year; the merged-in assets cost $15.09 to $18.63 a Boe and their production fell 18.0% in 2024; operating losses in 8 of 11 years 2015 to 2025, operating margin -46.6% against SM 12.0%, Civitas 21.5% pretax and Evolution Petroleum 19.6%; the first-half 2026 operating income of $22.1M came from price (about $64.10 a Boe realized against $50.27 in 2025), not cost. The Competition section names no company; the analyst took Civitas, SM Energy and Evolution Petroleum, named in Item 1 as basin operators and partners, as the named rivals and said so; each filer defines unit cost differently. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** Juniper 51.6% and Kukes 33.1% with a charter waiver of corporate opportunities to both; FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 restated and internal control not effective at 2025 year-end; 2019 related-party notes converted to paid-in capital; the chief accounting officer left in June 2026 and the chief executive in September 2026; in August 2026 the company agreed to pay a buyer $3.8M to take Pine Haven, a subsidiary bought nine months earlier; revolver $85M drawn at 2026-06-30 against a $125M borrowing base. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash (operating cash less stock pay less net capital spending) 757, 1,618, -13,183, -15,967 and -9,542 thousand 2021 to 2025, mean -$7.26M (-$0.83M on the depreciation variant); the 2025 deal paid more in cash ($115.6M) than in preferred ($64.2M), an acquisition, so the organic pair central; value about **$(15.58)** a share at both ends all-equity ($(10.06) equity-only); fair price about **$(11.06) all-equity** ($(5.46) equity-only), no positive price earning the floor; the combined companies beside still average negative; the first-half 2026 run rate shown beside as contrary evidence (about $18.56), not the convention's figure; not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing filtered on the run date showing ten other 2026-10-16 run names, not opened; the RCON commit subjects, two research-folder names and memory lines in the session context; none used. Commits 4108301b, 666fa632, 7fb5620a, 655363d9, four; the Q2 commit subject says "two to four times", the run file and close say 1.5 to 4.2. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for PED). Citations: the analyst's `check_citations.py` PASS (37 ids); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` no phantom, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) no rule for an acquisition that dwarfs the acquirer at the window's edge, and the serial-acquirer test fires trivially when owner cash before purchases is negative; (2) whether "named rivals" means named as competitors or named in the same basin; (3) no rule for comparing unit costs defined differently across filers; (4) `tools/run.py` took a vehicle-purchase tag as capital spending for this filer. Could not get: one cost definition across filers, the restated 2022 depletion, the acquired companies' stock pay, Continental Resources' filing status.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a high-cost producer in a commodity field; unit production cost 1.5 to 4.2 times Civitas's and SM Energy's in every year 2017 to 2025, the 2025 merged-in assets costlier still, operating losses in 8 of 11 years 2015 to 2025 against positive results at the basin neighbours; the 2026 first-half profit came from price, not cost. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: Juniper 51.6% and Kukes 33.1% with a corporate-opportunity waiver, three restated years and ineffective controls, CEO and CAO departures in 2026, $3.8M paid to dispose of a subsidiary bought nine months earlier. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash negative on the window, value and fair price below zero (fair about $(11.06) all-equity, $(5.46) equity-only) against $13.48, not armed. `tools/run.py` took a vehicle tag as capital spending for this filer; not used. Framework gaps for the operator: an acquisition that dwarfs the acquirer at the window's edge and the serial-acquirer test on negative owner cash; what "named rivals" means; unlike unit-cost definitions.
